tools.name: search
tools.description: Find value investors (managers) and companies on moatshark by name, person or ticker. Returns slugs for get_manager and get_company, and results with ids for fetch.

tools.name: get_manager
tools.description: Everything moatshark has on one value investor: its latest 13F (holdings, weights, change from the previous quarter), the overseas stakes a 13F never shows (from regulators in Japan, the UK, the Netherlands, France, Germany and Spain, with estimated values), its US funds' non-US holdings (N-PORT), 5

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: Which value investors hold a company, how their holdings changed, its directors' recent share purchases and sales (Form 4), and basic SEC company facts.

tools.name: latest_filings
tools.description: The newest 13F filings from the managers on moatshark, with each one's biggest buys and sales.

tools.name: quarter_roundup
tools.description: What the managers owned, bought and sold in one quarter (from 2013 Q1). Omit the quarter for the latest one being filed.

tools.name: filing_forecast
tools.description: When the managers file their 13Fs: the deadline for the quarter being filed, who has filed so far, who is expected on each remaining day (from each manager's last eight quarters), and who is later than usual. Give a slug for one manager's habit and history.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: The full record for one id from search (e.g. 'manager:berkshire-hathaway' or 'company:ko'), as text with its moatshark url.

tools.name: insider_buying
tools.description: Open-market share purchases reported on Form 4 in the last 90 days: by the value investors themselves (as 10% owners) and by companies' own directors and officers.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch · Private data: get_manager, filing_forecast, fetch · Public sink: get_company, insider_buying.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch · Private data: get_manager, filing_forecast, fetch · Public sink: get_company, insider_buying

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
